ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a schematic diagram of vertical circular motion, with A located at the lowest point of the circle and B located at the highest point of the circle. At point A there is a horizontal rightward velocity arrow, labeled V. The string length is labeled L, and the string points from the suspension point near the center of the circle to the position of the small ball on the circumference. θ is the angle made by the string relative to the downward vertical direction at point A. The figure also draws the vertical reference line passing through A and B. Then reason: The problem states that the horizontal velocity V at point A is just sufficient for the small ball to reach the highest point B. According to the critical condition for the string to remain taut in vertical circular motion, the minimum velocity at the highest point B satisfies v_B^2 = gL. By conservation of mechanical energy from A to B, B is 2L higher than A, so 1/2 M V^2 = 1/2 M v_B^2 + Mg(2L). Therefore V^2 = gL + 4gL = 5gL. At the position making an angle θ with the direction of the lowest point, the small ball rises relative to point A by h = L(1 - cosθ). Conservation of energy gives v_θ^2 = V^2 - 2gL(1 - cosθ) = 5gL - 2gL + 2gL cosθ = gL(3 + 2cosθ). The condition gives v_θ = V/2, so v_θ^2 = V^2/4 = 5gL/4. Thus gL(3 + 2cosθ) = 5gL/4, obtaining 3 + 2cosθ = 5/4, namely cosθ = -7/8. Because -7/8 is less than -√2/2, and θ is within the vertical circular angle range from 0 to π, θ is located in the interval of the second quadrant close to π, namely 3π/4 < θ < π.

raw_record.question_text: A bob of mass M is suspended by a massless string of length L. The horizontal velocity V at position A is just sufficient to make it reach the point B. If the speed of the bob at angle \(\theta\) is half of that at A, what is the range of \(\theta\)?

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to identify A as the lowest point of the vertical circle, B as the highest point, and \(\theta\) as the angle made by the string from the downward vertical position at A. From the text, the bob is on a massless string of length \(L\), has horizontal speed \(V\) at A, and this speed is just enough to reach B. Apply the critical condition for a string pendulum to complete the vertical circle: at the top B the minimum speed satisfies \(v_B^2=gL\), so by energy from A to B, \(V^2=v_A^2=5gL\). At an intermediate angle \(\theta\), the height above A read from the circular geometry is \(h=L(1-\cos\theta)\). Conservation of mechanical energy gives \(v_\theta^2=V^2-2gL(1-\cos\theta)=gL(3+2\cos\theta)\). The text condition says \(v_\theta=V/2\), so \(v_\theta^2=5gL/4\). Equating gives \(3+2\cos\theta=5/4\), hence \(\cos\theta=-7/8\). Since this angle lies in the quadrant where \(\cos\theta< -\sqrt2/2\), conclude \(3\pi/4<\theta<\pi\).
